newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper slightly down on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper slightly down on consolidation.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures opened slightly down on Friday in a mood of consolidation as copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) displayed some upward momentum overnight, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract opened at 22,230 yuan ($2,681) per tonne, down 20 yuan from Thursday's close. It fell further early in the session.
Traders said they expected the contract to meet support at the 22,000-yuan level with resistance at 22,400 yuan per tonne.
LME copper prices were sent back under $2,400 a tonne during late Thursday LME ring and kerb trading, although the market still concluded the session higher.
Prices were unable to clear resistance around $2,415, and the subsequent slippage under $2,400 suggested seven-week lows of $2,355 hit on Wednesday could come under attack again.
Last trade was at $2,398 a tonne, up $25 from Wednesday's kerb close.
Shanghai traders said that despite over-sold technical signs after recent plunges on the local market, a solid rebound was still impossible in the short term due to poor fundamentals.
The price of physical copper had fallen to around 21,800 to 22,000 yuan per tonne, against Thursday levels around 22,100 to 22,300 yuan, they added.
Aluminium opened mostly up. The key September 1997 contract rose 50 yuan to 13,950 yuan per tonne at the opening session.
